html:
"Sinic" is the map's label for the Chinese-speaking farming peoples of the Yellow River plain and beyond, around the core states, in 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE.

In these centuries the Shang and then the Zhou ruled the center, but many towns and peoples around them shared much of their way of life: millet in the north and rice further south, pigs and silk, bronze cast in clay molds, and the worship of ancestors. Writing appears with Shang oracle bones about 1200 BCE. Some neighbours had striking cultures of their own, such as the makers of the Sanxingdui bronzes in Sichuan.

Over the following centuries Zhou rule and then Qin unification in 221 BCE drew most of these peoples into one Chinese state and culture.
sum: "Sinic" is the map's label for the Chinese-speaking farming peoples of the Yellow River plain and beyond, around the core states, in 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE.
